# Search Methods for RAG ## Semantic search Semantic search compares embedding vectors. Two texts with similar meaning have vectors that point in a similar direction, which is measured with cosine similarity. Semantic search finds paraphrases well, for example matching "car" with "automobile", but it can miss exact terms such as error codes or product names. ## Keyword search with BM25 BM25 is a ranking function that scores documents by how often the query words appear in them, giving more weight to rare words and less weight to very long documents. It is excellent at exact matches but does not understand synonyms. ## Hybrid search Hybrid search runs semantic search and keyword search together and merges the two result lists. citations.text: # Large Language Model Basics ## Tokens Language models read and write text as tokens, which are pieces of words. In English, one token is roughly four characters, or about three quarters of a word. ## Context window The context window is the maximum number of tokens the model can read in one request, including the prompt, the retrieved passages and the answer. Passages that do not fit must be dropped, which is why retrieving the right passages matters more than retrieving many of them. ## Temperature Temperature controls randomness. A temperature of 0 makes the model pick the most likely token each time, giving repeatable answers, which is useful for evaluation. citations.text: # Evaluating a RAG System ## Retrieval metrics Recall@k is the fraction of questions for which at least one correct passage appears in the top k retrieved results. Recall@5 is the most common version. Mean Reciprocal Rank (MRR) averages 1 / rank of the first correct passage, so it rewards systems that put the right passage near the top. ## Answer metrics Faithfulness measures whether every claim in an answer is supported by the retrieved passages. It is often scored by a second language model acting as a judge. Answer correctness compares the answer with a reference answer written by a person. ## Refusal cases A good evaluation set includes questions whose answer is not in the documents.
